item.title: 'I gave everything that I had': Flydubai captain tells Netanyahu about co-pilot's hijacking attempt
item.description: The prime minister thanked Machchhar for his "remarkable" actions, saying that he "saved the spirit of the world."

item.title: IDF targets Yahya Sinwar's successor, Hamas Gaza leader Ali al-Amoudi, in strike
item.description: IDF attack helicopters and tanks struck targets in Gaza on Saturday in an operation aimed at killing Ali al-Amoudi, who succeeded Yahya Sinwar as Hamas's leader in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: Israel received full flydubai crew, passenger list prior to takeoff, source tells 'Post'
item.description: Several people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal on Friday that the UAE-based carrier flydubai hired the pilot despite concerns about his radicalization.

item.title: Flydubai aircraft reached near-supersonic speeds, extreme airframe stress levels - report
item.description: “I’m not sure it can ever be used again,” said Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University aerodynamicist Tony Farina, who has worked with the US Air Force and NASA on aviation-related projects.

item.title: Israelis celebrate Simchat Torah near Nova Festival site despite ban by police, KKL-JNF
item.description: The celebration follows a similar event at the site in 2025, which angered the families of October 7 attack victims. As a result, the JNF and police banned such events in 2026.

item.title: 'Attempted terror attack': UAE prosecution reveals first details of flydubai investigation
item.description: The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with an axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said.

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot was banned from flying in Oman after showing 'radical ideological views' - report
item.description: The report follows comments by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after the attempted hijacking, saying that the hijacker underwent radical Islamist indoctrination and was clearly suicidal.

item.title: Who will teach the next generation?
item.description: A Jerusalem summit will bring together more than 300 educators from Israel and around the world to share ideas, confront common challenges, and strengthen the connections that sustain Jewish life.

item.title: No. 1: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump: Remembering who brought the hostages home
item.description: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump helped achieve what few in Jerusalem thought possible, bringing every Israeli hostage home and reshaping the Middle East.

item.title: No. 3: Gadi Eisenkot: Israel’s next prime minister?
item.description: The former IDF chief has emerged as the leading opposition challenger to Netanyahu, offering voters a path to a post-Netanyahu Israel.

item.title: No. 4: Naftali Bennett: The former PM seeking a comeback to ‘repair Israel’
item.description: Since returning to politics, Bennett has shifted from his previous campaigns, taking a more liberal position while maintaining a strong right-wing stance on security.

item.title: No. 5: Ronald Lauder: Standing at the forefront of the fight against antisemitism
item.description: Lauder has never confined himself to quiet philanthropy - he continues to use his position to demand accountability from political leaders.

item.title: No. 2: Benjamin Netanyahu: Shaping Israel’s politics and global image for a generation
item.description: Netanyahu has become more than Israel’s prime minister for many. Abroad, for instance, he has become Israel’s symbol and the lightning rod for much of the hatred directed against the Jewish state.

item.title: Thailand revokes citizenship of Israeli businessman six years after naturalization
item.description: Thai authorities revoked the citizenship of Israeli-born Ariel Blushstein, citing his use of an Israeli passport after naturalization and an alleged failure to disclose Uruguayan citizenship.

item.title: One killed several wounded as settler extremists, Palestinians clash across West Bank during Sukkot
item.description: Clashes between settlers and Palestinians were reported across the West Bank during Sukkot, including a deadly shooting in Yasuf and violence linked to the olive harvest.

item.title: Jerusalem Biennale turns trauma and pain into art, healing, and hope
item.description: The Jerusalem Biennale showcases 42 exhibitions exploring trauma, memory, spirituality, healing, and the search for hope.

item.title: New Tel Aviv exhibition shows never-before-seen private work from six Israeli artists
item.description: A new exhibition at Tel Aviv University draws on the private archives of six major Israeli artists, presenting materials never shown before.

item.title: Al Jazeera speaks to Palestinian schoolboy from viral photograph
item.description: A photo went viral of a Palestinian boy hiding from Israeli forces on his way home from class in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: Israeli reporter’s ‘verbal attack’ ends Ireland football news conference
item.description: Israeli journalists asked coach Hallgrimsson about the Flydubai attack and alleged racist abuse by Ireland's players.

item.title: Somalia won’t accept Israeli presence ‘under any circumstances’: President
item.description: In exclusive Al Jazeera interview, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud says Israel planning a naval base in Berbera.
